detailLines: Prescott AZ NPP

SPECIAL ENTRY FEES: SR-$300 IF 1/$300 IF 2

GROUND RULES: Contestants who choose to enter the Legacy Steer Roping event must be at least 50 years old or a permit holder at the time of entry closing. They must also be entered in the steer roping event at the World's Oldest Rodeo. To be eligible, the contestant must not have been an NFSR qualifier during the past 3 years. Permit members of all ages will also be eligible to enter.

Contestants will pay an additional entry fees of $300. Contestants will not compete on any additional steers. The times that are recorded for the contestants' competition runs at the World's Oldest Rodeo will be used to determine the pay-off. Pay-off will only include the entry fees for the contestants who entered the Legacy Steer Roping through PROCOM. 6% will be held out of the total amount for the PRCA prior to the pay-off. Only the three go-rounds and the average after three go-rounds will be included in the pay-off for the Legacy Steer Roping. There will be no additional added money and since no additional animals will be run, there will be no additional stock charge or PROCOM charge.

Money won in the Legacy Steer Roping will not count towards PRCA World Standings, circuit standings, All Around standings, or for money won qualifications. It will count towards qualifying for the Legacy Steer Roping Finals held in conjunction with the National Finals Steer Roping. (NFSR qualifiers will not be eligible for the Legacy Steer Roping Finals).
STK CONT.: Various

(only contestants who competed in the first go-round will be placed in the performance). The remaining contestants (not placed in the performance) will run their second go-round in slack immediately following the completion of the first go-round in reverse order of their first go-round position. The order of the draw will be the same as the competition order. The contestants placed in the matinee performance on July 4 for their first go-round will compete during the night performance on July 4.

Money won in the Legacy Steer Roping will not count towards PRCA World Standings, circuit standings, All Around standings, or for money won qualifications. It will count towards qualifying for the Legacy Steer Roping Finals held in conjunction with the National Finals Steer Roping. (NFSR qualifiers will not be eligible for the Legacy Steer Roping Finals).

TR - The score length may be longer than Rulebook and a hand pulled barrier may be used with the Event Representatives approval after the animals to be used has been determined.

TD, SW, TR - If there are not enough contestants in the current year circuit money won category to fill the allotted circuit positions, the remaining positions will be filled with contestants from the previous year circuit money won category.

SR - Three go-rounds plus progressive. The first two go-rounds will be held during slack on Monday, July 6 at 6 PM. The third go-rounds will be held during slack July 7 at 8 AM. The top 30 (plus splits) advance to a progressive go-round held during the slack after the completion of the 3rd go-round. Extras will be used to replace sick or injured animals. (The misdraw procedure will not be used). Hand pulled barrier will be used. Length of score must be approved by Event Representative. $80 stock charge per go-round. Contestants who qualify for the progressive go-round will be responsible to pay an additional $80 stock charge for the progressive go-round.
QUALIFICATIONS: BB, SB, BR - 48 minimum entries. No compensation. No slack.

TD, SW, TR - 90 minimum entries (or teams). Two go-rounds. Back to back. The first go-round for each back to back group will be run at 8 AM on the day of the performance. The committee will have the option of designating two contestants (or teams) to compete during the performance that night for their second go-round. This designation must be made by the committee through PROCOM by 5 PM the first business day after the first go-round trade deadline. Also, the contestants with the top ten fastest times from the first go-round will be placed in the performance (slowest time will run first, fastest time will run last). The number of contestants placed in the performance will not exceed 10, unless one or both of the committee designated contestants are not among the top 10 from the first go-round (in this case the maximum could be 11 or 12). If the committee designated contestants are among the top 10, they will assume their position based on their first go-round time. If they are not among the top 10, they will run first in the performance (if neither of the two designated contestants are among the top 10, they will run first and second based on the reverse order of their first go-round positions). If splits result in more than 10, a random draw will determine which contestants will compete in the performance and which will compete in the slack. The order of competition of ties from the first go-round will also be determined by random draw. If there are not 10 qualified times from the first go-round to fill the performance, the remaining positions will be filled by contestants based on the reverse order of their first go-round positions (only contestants who competed in the first go-round will be placed in the performance).

The remaining contestants (not placed in the performance) will run their second go-round in slack immediately following the completion of the first go-round in reverse order of their first go-round. The order of the draw will be the same as the competition order.

TD, SW, TR - If a contestant qualifies for the finals at Casper and is placed in the Saturday morning slack at Sheridan, he will be allowed to compete on his second go-round animal immediately following the completion of the first go-round as long as he notifies the rodeo secretary prior to the stock draw for the second go-round. These contestants will compete first (and draw last) in the second go-round regardless of their first go-round times. The ten contestants or teams with the fastest times not including the contestants who qualify for the finals at Casper and request to be run first in slack, will be placed in the performance following the procedures outlined in the previous ground rules."

PERMITS:
FINALS: July 19- 1:00 PM BB SB BR TD SW TR
GROUND RULES: Only actual contestants and one companion allowed gate access.
ALL EVENTS: The "30-hour replacement" policy will be in effect. See Rodeo Entry Information page of the business journal.
ALL EVENTS - Re-entries will be accepted for available position on Wed., July 8 between 9 AM and 11 AM. See Rodeo Entry Information page of the business journal.
RIDING EVENT TRADE DEADLINE - Tue., July 7 at 4 PM. All confirmed trades will be final and will be processed immediately after both involved parties have confirmed through PROCOM.
TIMED EVENT TRADE DEADLINE - Thurs., July 9 at 4 PM. All confirmed trades will be final and will be processed immediately after both involved parties have confirmed through PROCOM.
ALL EVENTS - If contestant notifies a turnout prior to the 30-hour deadline for his competition time, turnout fines will be waived, if and only if he is replaced.
ALL CONTESTANTS - Secretary's office will be open from 12 noon to 4 PM on Weds. July 15.
ALL CONTESTANTS, STOCK CONTRACTORS, AND PERSONNEL - Must sign a release of liability with the secretary before participating.
ALL CONTESTANTS - Contestant parking will be open Monday, July 13 at 8 AM. No early entry.

ALL CONTESTANTS - If a contestant's actions are deemed detrimental to the PRCA, California Rodeo Salinas or the sport of rodeo in general, that contestant will not be eligible to compete at the California Rodeo Salinas in 2027.
RE - Any contestant who notifies a TO without a valid doctor's release or visible injury release will not be eligible to compete at the California Rodeo Salinas in 2026.
RE - Event representatives will have the opportunity to review the stock lists prior to the stock draw.
SLACK ORDER - Will be first go-round of LB, TD, SW, TR followed by second go-round of LB, TD, SW.

TE - If there are not enough contestants in the current year circuit money won category to fill the allotted circuit positions, the remaining positions will be filled with contestants from the previous year circuit money won category.

ALL CONTESTANTS WITH HORSES: All horses must be in compliance with current California Dept, of Food and Agriculture rules and requirements. Contestants who fail to comply with applicable health rules and requirements will be denied entry to the grounds or subject to removal from the grounds.
TE - If a timed event animal escapes (or a re-run is awarded for any other reason), the extra will be used. Only escaped animals go back into the herd.
TD - There will be a disqualification for a jerkdown as long as criteria are in compliance with the jerkdown policy.

ALL CONTESTANTS - If a contestant who qualifies for the finals notifies a turn-out, doctor's release or visible injury release through PROCOM, the contestant with the next highest ranking in the average may be contacted by PROCOM and placed in that available position. (Non-notified TO's and VIR's after the turn out deadline will not be replaced). If the next highest ranked contestant is not available to accept the position, the next highest ranked contestant may be contacted and placed in that position. This procedure will be followed until all positions are filled. The replacement contestants competition order will be based on his ranking in the average (not on the ranking of the contestant his is replacing). In the riding events, if an animal has already been drawn for a contestant who has turned-out, the replacement contestant will draw an animal from a pool consisting of all animals that have been turned-out (includes DR's and VIR's).
QUALIFICATIONS: BB & SB - 48 minimum entries. No compensation. No slack. One go-round W/F's (12 plus splits to 14). $5,000 held out for finals. No slack.
BR - 75 minimum entries. No compensation. No slack. One go-round W/F's (12 plus splits to 14). $5,000 held out for finals. There may be two sections during each performance. No slack.

TD - 90 minimum entries. Two go-rounds W/F's (12). Back to back, slack to slack, or slack to perf. Each day approximately 30 contestants will run their first go-round during slack. The top twelve fastest times from the first go-round each day will run their second go-round during the performance that day (slowest time will run first, fastest time will run last). If splits result in more than 12, a random draw will determine which contestants will compete in the performance (will not exceed 12) and which will compete in slack. The competition order of any ties from the first go-round will also be determined by random draw. If there are not 12 qualified times from the first go-round to fill the performance, the remaining positions will be filled based on the reverse order of their first go-round positions (only contestants who competed in the first go-round will be placed in the performances). The remaining contestants (not placed in the performance) will run their second go-round in that same slack (after the team roping) in reverse order of their first go-round positions. The order of the draw will be the same as the competition order. Scorelines will be 25'. Contestants will compete from left side of roping chute.

SW - 80 minimum entries. Two go-rounds W/F's (12). Back to back, slack to slack, or slack to perf. Each day approximately 35 contestants will run their first go-round during slack Thursday and Friday, 20 Saturday. The top twelve fastest times from the first go-round each day will run their second go-round during the performance that day (slowest time will run first, fastest time will run last). If splits result in more than 12, a random draw will determine which contestants will compete in the performance (will not exceed 12) and which will compete in slack. The competition order of any ties from the first go-round will also be determined by random draw. If there are not 12 qualified times from the first go-round to fill the performance, the remaining positions will be filled based on the reverse order of their first go-round positions (only contestants who competed in the first go-round will be placed in the performances). The remaining contestants (not placed in the performance) will run their second go-round in that same slack (after the team toping) in reverse order of their first go-round positions. The order of the draw will be the same as the competition order. Scorelines will be 25'. Contestants will compete from left side of roping chute.

TR - 120 minimum entries. Four go-rounds W/F's (12). Fifteen teams will run during the performance each day. The order of third and fourth go-round will be random draw. No trades allowed in the second and subsequent go-rounds. The entire fourth go-round will be run Sun, July 19 at 8 AM. Both contestants will compete from left side of roping chute. Cattle will be chute run (not drawn) if one head for every entry. Only two loops allowed per go-round. Scoreline will be 35'. Electric eye barrier will be used. Rule R3.1.1.1. and R3.3.6.1. will not be in effect.
STK CONT.: Corey & Lange Rodeo

VACCINATIONS: Every horse entering the enclosure of the racetrack must have been vaccinated by a veterinarian with an FDA approved modified live or killed virus vaccine specific for EHV-1 and EHV-4 and Influenza not less than 14 days and not more than 180 days prior to date of entry. The specific product used and expiration date as well as the date the horse was vaccinated must appear on the health certificate. Horses must be vaccinated no later than July 3, 2026.

ALL OTHER ANIMALS: All other animals will require a health certificate. No specific requirement on those but event hired veterinarian should know the information needed. Those should be completed by July 3, 2026. All health certificates with vaccination information and a negative Coggins test certificate must be submitted to Andrew Vold no later than July 16, 2026. Certificates can be submitted via email or photos of documents can be sent via text to the information. Andrew Vold at avold@canterburypark.com, 763-234-5966 (cell phone).
QUALIFICATIONS: BB, SB, BR - 36 minimum entries. No compensation. No slack.

For example, if contestants are trading between the 1st and the 4th days/performances, the trade deadline is 7:00 a.m. on day of 1st performance. If contestants are trading between the 2nd and 3rd days/performances, the trade deadline is 7:00 a.m. on the day of the 2nd performance. RE contestants' trade deadline is 12:00 p.m. (noon) each day.

In the TR, the top 30 headers and the top 30 heelers based on 2026 Payoff Series Standings who enter, and the top 10 headers and the top 10 heelers based on 2026 World Standings (as of July 6, 2026) who enter will be accepted. The 40 headers who are accepted as entries must rope with the 40 heelers who are accepted as entries. If a contestant's partner is drawn out due to qualification, a partner will be drawn from him by PROCOM from the other contestant's whose partners were drawn out due to qualifications.

FORMAT - BB, SB, BR: One go-round with a Finals. The top two (2) contestants based on highest scores from each of the first four (4) performances will advance to the Finals. Eight (8) contestants in the Finals.

The top 30 in each event based on 2026 Playoff Series standings, and the top 10 in the 2026 World standings as of July 6, 2026, entering will be accepted as entries. If the top 30 from the Playoff Series do not enter, the next highest ranked contestants from the 2026 World standings who enter will be accepted.

FORMAT - TD, SW, TR: Two go-rounds with a Finals. Back-to-back (10s each set.) Slack each morning and 2nd go round in performance each night. The top two (2) contestants based on average in that respective set will advance to the Finals.

Only cards accepted at gate will be contestants entered and 1 companion. All others must pay at the gate. No exceptions.

QUALIFICATIONS - Maximum 30 contestants based on top 100 blended CPRA/PRCA standings as of July 2, 2026 will be used to determine draw outs. If the qualifications are not filled by contestants with dollars won leaving open positions; the remaining openings will be filled by a random draw of card holders them semi-pro card holders. If there are still open positions, all remaining open positions will be filled by a random draw of permit holders.
FORMAT - One go-round with a (top 8) finals. $17,500 held out for short go, 8 places paid in long go, 8 places paid in aggregate, 4 places paid in short go.

FINALS - Top eight (8) will advance to finals. Top eight (8) will then pick their own finals stock out of pen of twelve (12). First (1st) place coming into the finals getting first pick down to eighth (8th). The remaining four (4) horses will be the finals re-rides (randomly drawn order). If there are not eight (8) qualified rides during the long go, all remaining positions will be filled by random draw. The eighth (8th) place is tied going into the finals, the tie will be broken by highest marked spur ride from the long go. If still tied, a random draw will determine the finals qualifier. Contestants who did not have qualified score in the first go-round and are drawn back to compete in the finals, will not be eligible to place in the aggregate.

RE-ENTRIES: Re-entries will be accepted for available positions at a time set by the CPRA after entries close to coincide with other entry schedules (typically all events for a particular weekend that require re-entries will be held on the same day) from 10 AM to 12 PM. See rodeo entry information on rodeo schedule. A contestant that re-enters will not be placed in a position that conflicts with his position at another CPRA rodeo or event. Additionally, if all spots are full on initial entry, a contestant that re-enters will be added to the alternate list (where accepted) but will be placed at the bottom of the list below those that entered on original entry day regardless of qualifications.
ALL EVENTS: Standardized Alternate Replacement Procedure will be in place for this event based on CPRA 2026 (standardized ground rules).
ALL EVENTS: Walk up replacement (implemented for 2026 season) will be in place for this event based on CPRA 2026 (standardized ground rules).

**Any contestant that is a replacement will be responsible for entry fees. Any contestant that notifies a doctor release, visible release, vet release, draw out, or a notified turnout will still be responsible for any entry fees they would incur regardless if replaced or not. Doctor releases are not responsible for entry fees as an example.

NOTE: In order for money won in the Hardgrass Bronc Match in Pollockville, AB to count for qualification for the 2026 National Finals Rodeo or the 2026 Rookie of the Year standings, a contestant must have entered and competed at a minimum of 40 PRCA rodeos during the 2026 season. Money won at Pollockville will not count towards All Around. Money won will also count towards X-Broncs standings.

GROUND RULES: Contestants who choose to enter the Legacy Steer Roping event must be at least 50 years old or a permit holder at the time of entry closing. They must also be entered in the steer roping event at the Newport Rodeo. To be eligible, the contestant must not have been an NFSR qualifier during the past 3 years. Permit members of all ages will also be eligible to enter.

Contestants will pay entry fees of $300. Contestants will not compete on any additional steers. The times that are recorded for the contestants' competition runs at the Dodge City Rodeo will be used to determine the pay-off. Pay-off will only include the entry fees for the contestants who entered the Legacy Steer Roping through PROCOM. 6% will be held out of the total amount for the PRCA prior to the pay-off. Only the three go-rounds and the average after three go-rounds will be included in the pay-off for the Legacy Steer Roping. There will be no additional added money and since no additional animals will be run, there will be no additional stock charge or PROCOM charge.

Money won in the Legacy Steer Roping will not count towards PRCA World Standings, circuit standings, All Around standings, or for money won qualifications. It will count towards qualifying for the Legacy Steer Roping Finals held in conjunction with the National Finals Steer Roping. (NFSR qualifiers will not be eligible for the Legacy Steer Roping Finals).
STK CONT.: Various

SLACKS: July 28- 8:00 AM ; July 29- 8:00 AM
EVENTS: BB SB BR TD SW @ $30000 TR-HD, TR-HL @ $30000 SR @ $15000
PERMITS: BB SB BR TD SW TR; MAX - SR
FINALS: August 2- 8:00 PM BB SB BR TD SW TR
GROUND RULES: ALL EVENTS - The "30-hour replacement" policy will be in effect. See the Rodeo Entry Information page of the Business Journal.
ALL EVENTS - The "walk-up replacement" policy will be in effect. See Rodeo Entry Information section of the business journal.
ALL EVENTS - Re-entries will be accepted for available positions on Tues., July 21 between 9 AM and 11 AM. See Rodeo Entry Information page of the business journal.
RIDING EVENT TRADE DEADLINE - Mon., July 20 at 4 PM. All confirmed trades will be final and will be processed immediately after both involved parties have confirmed through PROCOM.
TIMED EVENT TRADE DEADLINE - Thurs., July 23 at 4 PM. All confirmed trades will be final and will be processed immediately after both involved parties have confirmed through PROCOM.

ALL EVENTS - If a contestant who qualifies for the finals notifies a turn-out, doctor's release, or visible injury release through PROCOM, the contestant with the next highest ranking in the average may be placed in that available position. Non-notified turn-outs and visible injury releases after the turn-out deadline will not be replaced. If the next highest ranked contestant is not available to accept the position the next highest ranked contestant may be contacted and placed in that position. This procedure will be followed until all positions are filled. The replacement contestant's competition order will be based on his ranking in the average (not on the ranking of the contestant that he is replacing). In the riding events, if an animal has already been drawn for a contestant who has turned-out, the replacement contestant will draw an animal from a pool consisting of all animals that have been turned-out (includes DR's and VIR's).
GB - Approved for first slack event in accordance with R4.9.4.
TR - Only two loops allowed.

TD, SW, TR - If a contestant (or team) is a non-notified turn out in the first go-round, he will not be drawn an animal and will not be allowed to compete in the second go-round. The animal that was drawn for him for the first go-round that was turned out will be added back to the herd as "unused" and available to be drawn in a later pen."
SR - Three go-rounds. All will be run during slack on July 28 at 8 AM. Extras will be used to replace sick or injured animals. (The misdraw procedure will not be used). $80 stock charge per go-round.
QUALIFICATIONS: BB, SB - 48 minimum entries. No compensation. No slack. W/F's (12). $5,000 held out for finals. No slack.
BR - 80 minimum entries. No compensation. W/F's (12). $5,000 held out for finals. No slack.

TD, SW, TR - 90 minimum entries. Two go-rounds. W/F's (12). Back to back, slack to slack, or slack to performance. Approximately 30 contestants (or teams) will run their first go-round during 8 AM (held each day, Wed. July 29 - Sat. Aug. 1) immediately following the GB. The ten contestants with fastest times from the first go-round will be placed in the performance that night (slowest time will run first, fastest time will run last). If splits result in more than ten, a random draw will determine which contestants will compete in the performance (will not exceed ten) and which will compete in slack. The order of competition of ties from the first go-round will also be determined by random draw. If there are not ten qualified times from the first go-round to fill the performance, the remaining positions will be filled by contestants based on the reverse order of their first go-round positions (Only contestants who competed in the first go-round will be placed in the performance). The remaining contestants (not placed in the performance) will run their second go-round in slack immediately following the completion of the first go-round in reverse order of their first go-round position. The order of the draw will be the same as the competition order.
STK CONT.: Frontier Rodeo
SUB. CONT.: Double J Rodeo Company

QUALIFICATIONS: Maximum 30 contestants based on top 100 blended CPRA/PRCA standing as of July 6, 2026 up to and including Fort MacLeod. Ponoka's unofficial results will be used to determine draw outs if necessary. 10% (3) of contestants will consist of CPRA rookie or first year Pro members with 2026 earnings, blended with the CPRA and PRCA standings. If the qualifications are not filled by Full card contestants with dollars won leaving open positions; the remaining openings will be filled by random draw of card holders with no money won. If there are still open positions, all remaining openings will be filled permit holders with money won followed by a random draw of Permits with no money won.

FORMAT: One go-round with a (top 8) finals. $15,000 held out for short go, 6 places paid in long go, 4 places paid in short go (40%, 30%, 20%, 10%). Highest marked ride in the short go is crowned the event champion. No average shall be paid.

FINALS: Top eight (8) will advance to finals. Top eight (8) will draw (from hat or similar) their finals stock out of a pen of twelve (12). First (1st) place coming into the finals draws first down to eighth (8th). The remaining four (4) horses will be the finals re-rides (randomly drawn order). If there are not eight (8) qualified rides during the long go, all remaining positions will be filled by random draw. If the 8th place is tied going into the finals, the tie will be broken by highest marked spur ride from the long go, if still tied then a random draw will determine the finals qualifier.

**Any contestant that is a replacement will be responsible for entry fees. Any contestant that notifies a doctor release, visible release, vet release, draw out, or a notified turnout will still be responsible for any entry fees they would incur regardless if replaced or not. Doctor releases are not responsible for entry fees as an example.

RE-ENTRIES: Re-entries will be accepted for available positions at a time set by the CPRA after entries close to coincide with other entry schedules (typically all events for a particular weekend that require re-entries will be held on the same day) from 10 AM to 12 PM. See rodeo entry information on rodeo schedule. A contestant that re-enters will not be placed in a position that conflicts with his position at another CPRA rodeo or event. Additionally, if all spots are full on initial entry, a contestant that re-enters will be added to the alternate list (where accepted) but will be placed at the bottom of the list below those that entered on original entry day regardless of qualifications.
ALL EVENTS: Standardized Alternate Replacement Procedure will be in place for this event based on CPRA 2026 (standardized ground rules).
ALL EVENTS: Walk up replacement (implemented for 2026 season) will be in place for this event based on CPRA 2026 (standardized ground rules).
For additional ground rules see: "X-Broncs Ground Rules" in the Rodeo Entry Information section of the Business Journal.
STK CONT.: Various
